title: Israel’s President Taps Eisenkot, Not Netanyahu, to Form a Government
dek: Isaac Herzog chose opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot after parties recommended him over Benjamin Netanyahu, who remains caretaker prime minister while coalition talks begin.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Portrait of Israeli politician Gadi Eisenkot

keyPoints: President Isaac Herzog tasked Gadi Eisenkot with forming Israel’s next government after the October election left both major blocs short of a majority.
NPR reported that Herzog would formally hand Eisenkot the mandate at 5 p.m. local time on Sunday.
BBC and Al Jazeera reported that Eisenkot received 67 recommendations from incoming lawmakers and Netanyahu 46.
Eisenkot has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, to assemble at least 61 seats in the 120-member Knesset.
body:
Israel’s president has given opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a government, passing over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after last month’s election left neither bloc with a parliamentary majority.

## The mandate

[NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/07/g-s1-152536/netanyahu-israel-government-eisenkot-herzog) reported that President Isaac Herzog tapped Eisenkot, Netanyahu’s main rival, after parties representing most members of Israel’s parliament recommended that he try to assemble a coalition. NPR said Herzog would formally give Eisenkot the mandate at 5 p.m. local time on Sunday. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/7/israels-president-picks-eisenkot-over-netanyahu-to-form-next-government) reported that Herzog told Eisenkot of the decision on Saturday evening and that a spokesperson said the formal handover would come at a Sunday ceremony.

[BBC News](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cmy8367lj5xlo) said a statement from the president’s office reported that, after consultations with incoming Knesset members, Eisenkot received 67 recommendations for the premiership and Netanyahu 46. Al Jazeera reported the same 67-to-46 split, including endorsements from Arab-led parties. The BBC noted that the president has broad discretion and does not have to choose the leader of the party with the most seats.

Eisenkot wrote on X, “Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy,” the BBC reported.

## Why neither side won outright

NPR said Netanyahu’s Likud party won 27 seats in last month’s election, six more than Eisenkot’s Yashar party, but that neither secured a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. The BBC reported that Likud and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox allies won 53 seats, while Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc won 48.

Two Arab-led alliances, the United Arab List and the Joint List, together won 19 seats after a surge in turnout among Arab voters, the BBC said, positioning them as potential kingmakers. NPR said Palestinian citizens of Israel make up about 20 percent of the population and had a record turnout in these elections.

Al Jazeera, matching the BBC’s bloc totals, said Eisenkot’s four-party alliance won 48 seats and Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc 53, leaving both short of the 61 seats needed for a majority.

## The arithmetic ahead

Eisenkot will have 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, to put together a coalition, NPR and the BBC reported. That is up to six weeks to reach 61 seats.

The BBC said all but one of the Jewish parties pledged before the election not to work with the Arab-led lists. NPR reported that both Eisenkot and Netanyahu ruled out working with those parties before the vote, and that there is now public pressure on Eisenkot to change his mind.

Al Jazeera reported that winning over the ultra-Orthodox parties United Torah Judaism and Shas would give Eisenkot exactly 61 seats, and that he could also try to govern with fewer than 61 seats if he wins a parliamentary confidence vote. Those paths are political possibilities described by the outlets, not completed deals.

## Netanyahu’s warning

NPR said Netanyahu issued a video on Saturday warning against a partnership with Arab-led parties, calling them Hamas supporters and “those who oppose Judaism.” Eisenkot responded by calling the video hysterical, NPR reported.

Al Jazeera quoted Netanyahu as saying a government “dependent on Islamists” would “dismantle the state of Israel from within.” Those are Netanyahu’s claims; Meridian is not independently assessing them.

## Who Eisenkot is

NPR said Eisenkot is a former chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces, serving as the country’s top military commander from 2015 to 2019. He later joined Netanyahu’s emergency war cabinet after the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attacks, then left the following year, accusing Netanyahu of failing to make progress toward ending the Gaza war and securing the release of hostages, NPR reported. He lost his son, Gal, a reservist killed in Gaza, as well as two nephews during the war, according to NPR. He leads the center-right Yashar party, which he founded on an anti-corruption and government reform platform.

## If talks fail

If Eisenkot cannot form a government, Herzog can give another lawmaker a chance, NPR reported. If those efforts also fail, Israel could face another election, with Netanyahu remaining caretaker prime minister in the meantime. Al Jazeera said that if a second nominee fails, a parliamentary majority can back a third candidate for a final 14 days, and that if no government is formed a new election would be called within 90 days.

The BBC recalled that in 2020, after three deadlocked elections, Netanyahu and Benny Gantz agreed a power-sharing deal. Herzog, the BBC said, told parties during consultations that “not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled.”

## What is not yet known

Meridian has not confirmed the outcome of Sunday’s formal ceremony, which parties will join an Eisenkot-led coalition, or whether ultra-Orthodox or Arab-led factions will provide support. No coalition agreement had been announced in the reporting cited here.
